summary: New simultaneous quasi-uniform maximizing-sequence convergence and uniform integral tails on every bounded-test energy sublevel; finite maxima have energy and I error<=summable tails.
detailedSummary: One diagonal fast actual sequence has open exceptional sets of capacity<=8*2^(-3m)/7 on each fixed sublevel. Its Borel limsup is continuous on their closed complements; the exceptional set is null for every bounded MA/mixed measure and fixed-sublevel weak limit, and contains no full point. Uniform tail L1, energy/I and actual weak/moment controls make all finite maxima maximize for nu. Global USC/C/G recognition is not proved.
text:
One diagonal fast maximizing sequence gives quasi-uniform convergence and integral control of actual finite maxima. This uses only earlier own note n1, including its explicit conditional analytic-foundation and geometric-input boundary. Mu remains EVERY positive raw-mass-two finite-FULL-dual Radon measure, with arbitrary support.

Let C=C_mu be the universal maximizing-tail energy bound, delta_n=2^(-4n), beta_n=2^(-n), R_j=sum_(n>=j)delta_n. Choose r_n<=2^(-n) with T_(C+n+1)(r_n)<=delta_n. Choose actual normalized full competitors with deficits epsilon_n<=min(1,2^(-n),r_(n-1)/8,r_n/8), omitting r0. Coercivity puts all a_n in C_C. The midpoint bound gives I(a_n,a_(n+1))<=r_n. Thus for EVERY integer k>=1 and n>=k,
sup_(w in C_(C+k)) int|a_(n+1)-a_n|MA(w)<=delta_n.
It holds against nu too, by passing this fixed continuous absolute difference to the weak MA limit of the original maximizing family. Selection from a net needs only increasing indices for real deficits, never cofinality.

For Borel A define the actual set function Cap_L(A)=sup_(w in C_L)MA(w)(A). It is monotone and countably subadditive, of total value2. This is a set function of genuine bounded analytic MA measures, not an inverse operator or an assumed pluripotential capacity theorem. Set G_n={|a_(n+1)-a_n|>beta_n}, O_m=union_(n>=m)G_n. These are ordinary open, decreasing in m, and Markov plus subadditivity gives
Cap_(C+k)(O_m)<=sum_(n>=m)delta_n/beta_n=(8/7)2^(-3m)=P_m for m>=k.
Consequently N=intersection_m O_m is null for every bounded MA measure: normalize its test and choose k large enough. Every bounded mixed measure is also null on N, because B(p,q)<=2MA((p+q)/2), and normalization of that midpoint increases energy and leaves curvature unchanged.

It is null for EVERY weak limit lambda of MA measures from a fixed C_L. Here is the full compact-Hausdorff argument: for any ordinary open O, regularity and Urysohn express lambda(O) as the supremum of int h lambda over continuous 0<=h<=1 supported in O. Each integral is the weak limit of integrals bounded by Cap_L(O), so lambda(O)<=Cap_L(O). Apply this to O_m with k such that L<=C+k, then let m increase. In particular nu(N)=0. An actual atom MA(w_x)>=alpha_x delta_x at a full point has its normalized test in some C_(C+k). Were x in N, alpha_x<=Cap_(C+k)(O_m)<=P_m for all late m, impossible. N contains NO full point.

Outside O_m, every increment from index m on is<=beta_n. For q>=n>=m telescoping gives |a_q-a_n|<=sum_(l>=n)beta_l=2^(1-n), uniformly on the closed compact X\O_m. The restrictions therefore converge uniformly to a finite continuous function there. Define on all X the actual Borel extended-valued u=limsup_n a_n. It equals that continuous limit off O_m, is finite on X\N, and agrees with the family-independent ell at every full point. This is quasi-uniform convergence for EACH fixed bounded-test energy sublevel, without metrizability or countable points/tests. It is not global USC or psh recognition.

For h_j=sum_(n>=j)|a_(n+1)-a_n|, countable Tonelli gives sup_(w in C_(C+k))int h_j MA(w)<=R_j for j>=k. The same holds against nu. Define actual finite maxima M_(j,q)=max(a_j,...,a_q) and bounded finite LSC S_j=sup_(n>=j)a_n. Outside N, total variation is finite and |a_n-u|<=h_n<=h_j. Consequently, uniformly for all q>=j and all such w,
int|a_j-u|MA(w), int|M_(j,q)-u|MA(w), int(S_j-u)MA(w), int(S_j-a_j)MA(w)<=R_j.
The same bounds hold for nu. Null-set values are assigned arbitrarily in the integrals. In particular u is integrable against every bounded MA/mixed measure and nu, and int u nu=p. No claim integrates h_j against arbitrary prescribed mu.

The finite maxima are actual members of C_C. Tangent at a_j and their actual order give
0<=E(M_(j,q))-E(a_j)<=int(M_(j,q)-a_j)MA(a_j)<=R_j.
Green and order also give the STRONGER I bound
0<=I(a_j,M_(j,q))=int(M_(j,q)-a_j)[MA(a_j)-MA(M_(j,q))]<=R_j.
For every fixed test w, the genuine MA discrepancy is thus<=sqrt(12L R_j). Density and mass2 give uniform weak convergence to nu, for ALL q>=j as j tends to infinity. The n1 moment estimates give uniform reference/self-mixed/diagonal limits equal to those of a_j; the diagonal error is<=H_C(R_j)+sqrt(12C R_j). If d=E(M)-Ea_j and z=int(M-a_j)nu, both lie in[0,R_j]; hence |Fnu(M)-Fnu(a_j)|=|d-z|<=R_j. ALL these finite maxima uniformly maximize the full dual of nu.

For fixed j their energies increase with q; L_j=sup_q E(M_(j,q)) exists and satisfies Ea_j<=L_j<=Ea_j+R_j. Comparing M_(j+1,q)<=M_(j,q) proves L_j decreases, and the bounds prove L_j tends to e. This independently reconstructs and strengthens the entire ROOT finite-tail-maximum deduction. It assigns no E(S_j), no generated positivity to S_j, and no MA to the Borel u. Theorem new:diagonal and new:tails in standalone.tex contain the complete proofs. Original representability and prescribed-measure existence remain unresolved.
